On it. Initial findings from traces/Grafana: sudden spike in prefix cache miss ratio around 09:04:58 UTC correlated precisely with p99 climb. Cache hit rate for prefix keys dropped from 97% -> ~38% for ~6 minutes. See dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/abc123/hosted-api-p99?panelId=7

Logs (attached small sample) show many cold-KV reads and a burst of synchronous warmups that blocked token-serving threads. Error rate increase appears to be a direct consequence of timeouts while warmups were happening.

Immediate mitigation options:
- Roll back the TTL/shard rebalancing change that rolled out at 08:58 (if still active)
- Kick an async warmup job to pre-populate the hot prefixes (low risk)
- Temporarily increase worker threads that handle KV warmups

I'll attach logs and a 1-page p99_report for customer (p99_report_0719.pdf). Attaching logs_prefix_miss_20260719.tar.gz (stripped).

-Sean
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: cache miss correlation — quick RCA notes

Quick technical notes from infra: we pushed a shard rebalancing + reduced prefix-cache TTL experiment at 08:58 as part of a rollout intended to reduce memory pressure on the KV layer. The rebalancing triggered a coordinated invalidation of several prefix shards.

Two observations:
1) The invalidation caused a flood of synchronous KV reads when live requests hit now-cold prefixes. Our warmup path is currently synchronous for these keys, so token-serving threads were blocked waiting on KV.
2) Compaction on the KV store ran shortly after due to the same maintenance window which increased read latencies for background warmups.

Proposed mitigations (short-term):
- Revert the TTL/rebalancing experiment immediately (I have the rollback ready).
- Switch warmup to async path for affected prefixes and queue low-priority warmups (patch attached: proposed_patch_increase_warmup.sh).
- Increase the concurrency cap for warmup workers from 4 -> 12 for the next 24h to catch up.

Longer term: add canary gating for prefix invalidations, add synthetic warmup for critical prefix footprints, and add an observability alert specifically on cache-cardinality-change rate.

I'll stand by to push rollback once leadership signs off the immediate customer messaging.

-Hannah

Folks — brief executive note to summarize the incident and next steps for approval.

Timeline
- 08:58 UTC: rollout of shard rebalancing + reduced prefix-cache TTL (experiment)
- 09:04:58 UTC: Coordinated prefix invalidation observed; cache-hit-rate collapsed for ~6 minutes
- 09:05-09:12 UTC: p95/p99 spikes and temporary error-rate increase (~2.2%), several customer jobs timed out
- 09:18 UTC: SRE engagement and initial mitigations
- 09:30 UTC: rollback and async warmup started; metrics began returning to baseline by ~09:45

Impact
- A small set of customer production traffic (Acme) observed elevated latencies and transient errors for ~10 minutes. No data loss.

Actions taken
- Rollback of the rollout done by Hannah (rollback completed 09:30)
- Async warmup and increased warmup concurrency applied (see attached patch)
- Customer notified; CS offered credit and RCA within 48h

Proposed next steps (asking for approval):
1) Formalize a canary gate for any prefix invalidation/TTL change (engineering to scope effort)
2) Add an automated monotonic-alert for sudden large flips in prefix-cardinality cache hit rate
3) Approve issuing a 1-month service credit to Acme for the affected window (we proposed this to the customer; they requested credit in email)

Please reply with approve / need more detail. If approved, Laura can coordinate the commercial credit and Marissa will finalize the customer RCA doc.

-Rishi Malhotra
VP, Sales Ops (acting)
